reason: The text depicts Yahweh as an engaged, responsive God who actively cares for those who fear and obey Him. The midwives 'feared God' (v. 17), which motivated their moral disobedience to Pharaoh. In response, God 'dealt well with the midwives' (v. 20) and 'made houses for them' (v. 21) because of their reverence. This depicts a reciprocal, relational God who directly blesses and rewards human faithfulness—the opposite of remote or emotionally removed. The God shown here is morally engaged and responsive to human behavior, not distant or detached.
